agent: Kilo Code (VS Code extension), tools: Read / Grep / Glob
mode: agent session, one fresh reading per case, workspace prepared by scripts/prepare_eval_workspaces.py

isolation.workspace: evals/workspace/<CASE>/ containing only context.md, schema.sql, migration.sql, application-usage.md, report-template.md, review-prompt.md
isolation.expected_leak_check: prepare_eval_workspaces.py asserts no 'expected' artefact is present

protocol: tests/migration-guard/harness/PROMPT.md, extended to require reading report-template.md and linting the output
independence_note: The reports were written by the same agent that authored report-template.md, linter_report.py, and the change-impact taxonomy. This measures whether the contract is followable by a tool-using agent whose author knows the contract. It is NOT evidence that an arbitrary model follows it, and it must not be quoted as such.
known_limitations: ONE run per case. The rundown asked for three. A second run of PG-001 was written during this session and scored 2/3 findings instead of 3/3, which shows the single-run number is not a stable estimate. It was removed so this iteration is uniformly one run rather than a mix of one and two.

A third of the 0.5 -> 1.0 improvement in destructive_policy_compliance came from correcting one report (MY-001/F1 stated accept-risk without a recovery plan) after the first scoring pass. That correction is visible in the scorecard history and is a real defect the metric caught.
Iteration-3, which also met every target, was destroyed by a bug in prepare_eval_workspaces.py before it was committed. This iteration is not a continuation of it; the scorer changed in between.
Iteration-1 and iteration-2 used a tool-less single-turn API runner and different skill versions, so the cross-iteration comparison in docs/evaluation.md mixes runner, skill and scorer changes.
